BASELINE REMEASURED LIVE and reproduced v1 exactly: real 628, insns T857/O855, multiset 6t (target-only +2 b +1 li +1 mr, ours-only -2 addi). No drift.

PROBE D1 (REVERTED, REGRESSED, and it is the discipline-6 JOINT probe of two axes each measured negative alone): `#pragma opt_lifetimes off` inserted immediately above `int loadGauntletSave(void)` (its `reset` already stands at line 1420) TOGETHER WITH `s32 volatile bigSize; u8* volatile dirTab; char** volatile opts; void* volatile removedCb;` -> the same four WITHOUT `volatile` (neededPct left volatile). real 628 -> 962, insns T857/O863, multiset 12t. WORSE THAN EITHER AXIS ALONE (v1 probe 4 = 910 for the de-volatile alone; v1 probe 2 = 628 for the pragma deletion alone). The joint axis is dead, held_fixed = everything else in the TU.

PROBE D2 (REVERTED, REGRESSED): aggregate homing - replaced the four scalars with `struct { void* removedCb; char** opts; u8* dirTab; s32 bigSize; } lg;` (member order REVERSED so ascending member addresses would land removedCb@168 / opts@172 / dirTab@176 / bigSize@180 = the target map) and rewrote all 10 use sites to `lg.<member>`. real 628 -> 914, insns T857/O859, multiset 10t. INFORMATIVE NEGATIVE: the aggregate WAS memory-homed (so aggregates are a working homing mechanism without volatile), but MWCC scalarized it - the four landed at 184/188/192/196 in an order that is neither declaration nor reverse-declaration order - AND the frame GREW 288 -> 312 because a `lwz r3,192(r1); addi r0,r3,-23992; stw r0,164(r1)` loop-invariant temp was hoisted into the prologue.

PROBE D3 (REVERTED, REGRESSED, but the BEST of the three and the informative one): de-volatile ALL FIVE, i.e. `s32 volatile bigSize; u8* volatile dirTab; char** volatile opts; void* volatile removedCb;` and `u32 volatile neededPct;` -> the same five with no qualifier. real 628 -> 754, insns T857/O857 (COUNT EXACT), multiset 8t. The LOWER half of the frame then matched the target EXACTLY - checkMsg@148, flags@152-154, fileNo@156, keepgrp@160-162 - and the whole residual collapsed onto the prologue block. What broke it: MWCC hoisted `bigSize - 23992` (the checksum loop's init expression) into the function prologue as `lwz r3,172(r1); addi r0,r3,-23992; stw r0,144(r1)`, consuming slot 144 (neededPct's home in the target) and pushing the four into spill-allocation order 164=removedCb/168=dirTab/172=bigSize/176=opts with the float-magic temp displaced to 180.
attributes.residual:
BEST RETAINED: UNCHANGED at real 628, insns T857/O855, multiset 6t. No source change kept this run; the value delivered is the decoded map plus three closed axes.

MECHANISM D, NOW FULLY DECODED (this run's main finding, and it CORRECTS v1's census). Every (r1) slot below 190 was tallied from both raw objects (LG_scratch/slots.py: regex over `fnasm` target vs --ours, counting op kinds per displacement). The correspondence is EXACT and total:
  TARGET (descending)  180 bigSize | 176 dirTab | 172 opts | 168 removedCb | 164 float-magic 0x43300000 cache (1 stw + 2 lwz, feeding the int->double temp at 184/188) | 162,161,160 keepPair/keepSerial/keepSerial2 | 156 fileNo | 154,153,152 found/needUnmount/needCheck | 148 checkMsg | 144 neededPct | 140,136 serial[1],serial[0] | 128 memSize.
  OURS (descending)    180 float-magic | 176,177,178 keepgrp | 172 fileNo | 168,169,170 flags | 164 checkMsg | 160 bigSize | 156 dirTab | 152 opts | 148 removedCb | 144 neededPct | 140,136 serial | 132 memSize.
READ: the TARGET's local block is a SINGLE block in pure declaration order, and our source's declaration order ALREADY reproduces it exactly (bigSize, dirTab, opts, removedCb, [compiler temp], keepPair, keepSerial, keepSerial2, ...registers..., fileNo, found, needUnmount, needCheck, checkMsg, neededPct). Our ONLY defect is that MWCC segregates `volatile` locals into their own sub-block and places it BELOW the non-volatile one, so our two sub-blocks are correctly ordered INTERNALLY but SWAPPED as groups. v1's claim that neededPct is misplaced is WRONG - neededPct@144 is correct on both sides, by coincidence of our volatile block's bottom. memSize (128 vs 132) is the one remaining low-region defect, not previously noted.
  COST OF MECHANISM D: exactly 36 instructions carry a differing (r1) displacement (sum of the per-slot counts above), i.e. about 72 of the 628 real - the largest NAMED item but NOT the majority. The majority is a register-colour cascade (regnorm: 1025 paired, 106 renaming, 44 genuine STRUCTURAL after removing 109 branch-displacement artifacts, 84 unpaired).
  WHY IT IS HARD, precisely: the volatile scaffold is not merely a slot-placement hack - it also reproduces the target's REGISTER ALLOCATION (both sides use the full callee-saved set, stmw r14). Removing volatile hands those four registers back to the allocator, which then (a) enregisters the four (D1/D3) and evicts whatever the target kept, and (b) frees the front end to hoist `bigSize - 23992` because the value is no longer memory-qualified. So MECHANISM D needs a form that is memory-homed, NOT loop-invariant-hoistable, and NOT segregated - and `volatile` is the only qualifier that gives the first two while being the sole cause of the third.
  NEXT UNTRIED HYPOTHESIS (mandatory step 1 for the next lane, per discipline 10b): D3 is one hoist away from a clean base. Block the `bigSize - 23992` prologue hoist WITHOUT volatile - e.g. move the checksum loop's bound into a form MWCC will not hoist (recompute the subtraction inside the loop guard, or sink the whole `{ u32 saved; ... }` block's declarations so the expression is first evaluated after a call), then re-run D3. If the hoist dies, D3's slot map should become the target's outright, since D3 ALREADY matched the lower half exactly at count parity 857/857.
